amendments.normalized_body: In `gh_mineral_factor()` (shrimp.rs:1639-1641), the floor value 0.3 is hardcoded in both the low-GH and high-GH branches, while the parallel `molt_mineral_modifier()` (shrimp.rs:1690) uses the tunable `params.molt_mineral_factor_floor`. If a user tunes `molt_mineral_factor_floor` to a different value, molt and reproduction GH penalties will diverge silently. Either: (a) add a dedicated `repro_mineral_factor_floor` parameter, or (b) reuse `molt_mineral_factor_floor` in `gh_mineral_factor()` and document that it controls both domains.

In `tan_repro_factor()` (shrimp.rs:1619) and `no2_repro_factor()` (shrimp.rs:1630), the slope of suppression is computed as `threshold * 2.0`, meaning full suppression always occurs at 2× the threshold concentration. This implicit doubling rule is not exposed as a tunable parameter. Add explicit `tan_repro_full_suppression_mg_n_per_l` and `no2_repro_full_suppression_mg_n_per_l` parameters (defaulting to 2.0 and 1.0 respectively) so the suppression curve shape can be tuned independently of the onset threshold.

In `temp_repro_factor()` (shrimp.rs:1546-1549), the cold-temperature offset `4.0` (which defines the width of the ramp from 0.1 to 1.0 below `optimal_temp_min_c`) is hardcoded. Similarly, the piecewise slopes 0.5 and 0.45 (lines 1554, 1557) and the minimum values 0.1 and 0.05 (lines 1547, 1559) are all hardcoded. These shape the temperature-reproduction curve but cannot be tuned via species data. At minimum, document these as intentionally fixed; ideally, extract the cold-offset width as a named parameter.

In `gh_mineral_factor()` (shrimp.rs:1641), the high-GH penalty divisor is hardcoded as `10.0`: `(1.0 - (gh_d - params.gh_max_d) / 10.0)`. The molt system has a tunable `molt_gh_excess_penalty_divisor` for the analogous calculation. Use a corresponding named parameter for the reproduction GH excess curve.

Current diff is solving the wrong task. The touched implementation is limited to alkalinity accounting (`crates/tank_core/src/systems/nitrogen_cycle.rs:12`, `crates/tank_core/src/systems/water_change.rs:128`, `crates/tank_core/src/types/process.rs:10`) plus alkalinity-focused tests, but there is still no corresponding change in the shrimp reproduction pipeline/spec data requested by `tanksim-6e5.6.4`. As submitted, none of the required breeding-suppression, egg-dropping, or 2000-hour reproduction scenario acceptance criteria are implemented.

`crates/tank_core/src/systems/nitrogen_cycle.rs:346` computes `total_mg_n_nitrified` as `nob_step.oxidized_n_mg + comammox_step.oxidized_n_mg`, while `crates/tank_core/src/engine.rs:232` records that field as the tick's total nitrification. That omits AOB TAN->NO2 oxidation whenever nitrite accumulates, even though that pathway is the one consuming alkalinity/O2. In low-NOB or low-DO scenarios the new trace will therefore report low nitrification while `alk_consumed_meq` shows the opposite.

`crates/tank_core/tests/nitrification_alkalinity.rs:1` contains the new regression coverage, but the file is still untracked, so it is absent from `git diff` and would not ship with the patch as reviewed. The submitted change therefore adds runtime behavior without actually delivering the promised test coverage.
